instruction:
Use the USGS Water Science School to compare pH, turbidity and electrical conductivity as different descriptions of water. Open pH and Water, Turbidity and Water, and Conductivity (Electrical Conductance) and Water. For each, state what is measured, identify the measurement method or instrument described, and give one written explanation of what can change it. Report the pH scale’s neutral point and logarithmic interpretation, turbidity’s stated measurement unit, and why pure water and water containing dissolved ions differ in conductivity. End by distinguishing suspended particles from dissolved ions and explaining why these measurements should not be treated as interchangeable. Cite all three articles. This is a comparison of documented properties, not an experiment or an assessment of any actual sample’s drinkability.

Stopping condition: Stop when a three-property comparison and the requested scale, unit and particle/ion distinctions are supported by the three USGS articles, without assessing a real sample.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate if the agent provided the required details for pH from the USGS article. Full credit if the agent states what is measured, identifies the measurement method/instrument described, gives one explanation of what can change it, reports the pH scale's neutral point, and explains the logarithmic interpretation. Full credit is also awarded if the agent attempts to access the pH article but the site is down/inaccessible, or if specific details are missing from the current live page and the agent notes this. Partial credit if some available elements are missing.

Evaluate if the agent provided the required details for turbidity from the USGS article. Full credit if the agent states what is measured, identifies the measurement method/instrument described, gives one explanation of what can change it, and reports the stated measurement unit. Full credit is also awarded if the agent attempts to access the turbidity article but the site is down/inaccessible, or if specific details are missing from the current live page and the agent notes this. Partial credit if some available elements are missing.

Evaluate if the agent provided the required details for electrical conductivity from the USGS article. Full credit if the agent states what is measured, identifies the measurement method/instrument described, gives one explanation of what can change it, and explains why pure water and water containing dissolved ions differ in conductivity. Full credit is also awarded if the agent attempts to access the conductivity article but the site is down/inaccessible, or if specific details are missing from the current live page and the agent notes this. Partial credit if some available elements are missing.

items.criterion: Distinguish suspended particles from dissolved ions and explain non-interchangeability
items.description: Evaluate if the agent correctly distinguishes suspended particles from dissolved ions and explains why these measurements (pH, turbidity, conductivity) should not be treated as interchangeable based on the gathered information. Full credit if both elements are clearly addressed, or if the agent provides a logical explanation based on the information it could successfully retrieve. Partial credit if only one is addressed when information for both was available.

items.criterion: Cite all three articles and adhere to task constraints
items.description: Evaluate if the agent cited all three specified USGS Water Science School articles (or noted if any were inaccessible) and adhered to the constraint of comparing documented properties without assessing an actual sample's drinkability or acting as an experiment. Full credit for citing all three sources and maintaining the required theoretical scope. Partial credit if citations are incomplete or if the agent unnecessarily includes an assessment of a real sample.
